thread:
Sahil: Heads-up — I'm sketching an operator flow for automatic fallback that includes a reversible rollback and a clear, auditable reason. Need quick opinions on UX constraints.
Maya: love it. can you outline the must-haves? rollback == operator-triggered revert, or automatic?
Sahil: both. must-haves: 1) immutable 'why' blob that links to telemetry (p95, 5xx, hallucination classifier), 2) one-click rollback in console with preflight check, 3) clear sticky-override semantics + TTL, 4) audit entry with who/when/reason.
Liam: ergonomics note — if rollback flips routing back to primary model, we need a canary window + sampling toggle to avoid immediate re-fallback oscillation.
Priya: agree. also want a dry-run button that replays last 5k requests through the target model variant and surfaces diffs. low-cost sample only.
Jonah: UI idea — show a compact timeline: Trigger -> Metric spike snapshot -> Samples (3) -> Rollback button. keep it one row so operators can scan fast.
Sahil: good. question: should rollback produce a compensating audit event that mirrors the fallback event? ops people asked for explicit pairing in the audit log.
Maya: yes, pairing helps forensic queries. store pair_id and a short human reason field. we should limit freeform text to 200 chars.
Liam: implementation detail — the 'why' blob should include rule_id + trigger_snapshot + model_variants. That way we can reconstruct routing decisions without storing full requests.
Priya: and include a telemetry link 'why-did-you-fallback' that opens a pre-filtered trace in sandbox. ops-bot can log the link when fallback occurs.
ops-bot: fallback detected: rule=fallback_low_latency, snapshot_id=fb-2026-03-15-42, traces_link=https://console/redwood/traces/fb-2026-03-15-42 :bell:
Jonah: a couple of UX edgecases — what if operator does rollback but traffic profile changed? we should surface 'risk' badges: LikelySafe / MediumRisk / HighRisk based on recent signal divergence.
Sahil: agreed. also we need policy-level tolerances: e.g., silent-degrade (no user-visible change), soft-degrade (reduced quality with banner), full-degrade (swap model). Rollback semantics differ per mode.
Maya: product prefers default rollback to 'previous stable variant' and an opt-in for 'force revert to last known config'.
Liam: telemetry-wise, add a TTL on sticky overrides. if operator overrides for >24h we emit an alert and require justification in the audit entry. cuts down on forgotten overrides.
Priya: for the dry-run diff, we should include token-cost delta and a small quality score (bleu-ish / classifier score) so SREs can justify cost vs quality tradeoff quickly.
Sahil: edge ops ask: can we support rollback from mobile console? need same audit guarantees. probably surface a limited rollback UX for mobile with coarser info.
Jonah: yes, mobile should show compact reason + one-tap rollback + 'more info' that opens the full trace in desktop.
Maya: two followups: 1) what fields are required for the immutable audit? I'm thinking pair_id, trigger_ts, rule_id, trigger_snapshot_id, model_from, model_to, operator, action (auto/manual/rollback), justification. 2) retention policy? 1 year?
Liam: those fields sound right. for retention, 1 year by default, enterprise option for longer. but make exports easy (CSV/JSON).
Priya: security note — redact user-level PII from the stored snapshot. only include hashed request ids for replay mapping.
Sahil: perfect. last thing — rollout automation: if auto-fallback flips to variant B then auto-rollout back to A after health checks pass, should that be allowed? ops want a guard: only if automatic fallback was not operator-overridden.
Maya: agree. add a 'no-auto-revert' flag set when operator manually rolls back.
ops-bot: logged: design-decisions noted -> pairing audit, TTL overrides, dry-run replay, risk badges. Created ticket PLAT-1182.
Sahil: awesome. I'll draft a quick console mock and PR the audit schema. thanks all.
Maya: TY!
Liam: +1
Priya: :thumbsup:
